name: Field Doctor-Style Potato Topped Chicken Pie (Low FODMAP)
ingredients:
525 g Sliced Potatoes
525 g Chicken
320 g Oyster Mushrooms
2 medium Carrots
1/4 medium Swedes
160 g Celeriac (CELERY)
160 g Soy Milk [SOY beans, water]
160 g Spinach
3 tbsp Tapioca Starch
3/4 tbsp White Miso [SOYA beans, cultured rice, sea salt, water]
5 tbsp Mixed Herbs
pinch of Chicken Stock (Chicken Extract, Chicken Fat, Salt], Forest Mix Mushrooms, Parsley Flat, Sea Salt, Chive Rings, Black Pepper
directions:
1. Potato topping: Par-boil sliced potatoes until just tender; drain and toss with a little extra virgin olive oil, salt and chives.

2. Filling: Soften carrot, swede, celeriac and chives in extra virgin olive oil. Add oyster mushrooms and forest mushrooms; cook until moisture cooks off. Stir in diced chicken and cook until sealed.

3. Sauce: Add soy milk, chicken stock, white miso, herb mix and pepper. Simmer until chicken is cooked; thicken with tapioca starch slurry to a pie-filling consistency. Fold in spinach until wilted. Season with sea salt.

4. Assemble & bake: Fill oven dish(es), overlap potato slices on top, drizzle with oil. Bake at 190°C fan for 25–35 minutes until golden and bubbling.
 
Cool, portion into 8, refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze; reheat until piping hot.

Home recreation inspired by Field Doctor Potato Topped Chicken Pie (Low FODMAP) (~420 g ready meal). Scaled to 8 portions. Not an official Field Doctor recipe. https://www.fielddoctor.co.uk/products/potato-topped-chicken-pie
notes:
REVERSE-ENGINEERED from Field Doctor published ingredients for personal home cooking only. Official meal is Monash Low FODMAP certified at single-serve size.

Scaling notes
Scaled for 8 portions from Field Doctor single serve (~420 g x 8 = 3360 g).
Unlabelled amounts inferred from UK descending-weight ingredient order (each item <= the one above and >= the one below; leftover mass shared on that basis, not equally).
Spoon measures use ingredient density (g per tsp) then round to kitchen fractions.
Amounts above 50 g are rounded to the nearest 5 g for cooking convenience.
Sweet peppers ~140 g each; carrots ~80 g; sweet potatoes ~130 g; courgettes ~175 g; aubergines ~250 g; swedes ~800 g; plum tomatoes = 400 g tins; lemon ~45 ml / lime ~30 ml juice.
Duplicate label ingredients merged (higher amount kept).
Liquid for home cooking: cook rice, quinoa, pasta, noodles and potatoes in water as you normally would (salt the water; drain where appropriate). For sauces, braises and stir-fry glazes, add water or stock gradually until the consistency is right — do not try to measure the ready-meal's residual water.
Low FODMAP: no onion or garlic bulbs — use chives / green tops only. Inspired recreation from Field Doctor ingredients, not an official recipe.
Chives listed in grams to match fresh packs (e.g. Waitrose Cooks' Ingredients Chives, 20 g).
Ready-meal residual water was ~523 g (inferred ~15.57% from list order) and is not listed as an ingredient.
Oil for home cooking: where Extra Virgin Olive Oil was only a cooking fat on the label, it is omitted from ingredients — fry, soften, sear or roast in extra virgin olive oil as needed. It is kept as an ingredient on richer/oil-forward dishes (e.g. pesto-style sauces or high oil content).
Ready-meal residual Extra Virgin Olive Oil was ~48 g (inferred ~1.43% from list order) and is treated as cooking fat (fry in extra virgin olive oil) rather than a measured ingredient.
